title: Hybrid prefetch holdback and kernel-splitting for heterogeneous-head models (Qwen/Llama)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce a hybrid prefetch holdback and model-aware kernel splitting to reduce KV fragmentation and tail latency for heterogeneous-head models (Qwen/Llama). No user-facing API changes. Performance improvement for MQA/GQA workloads; rollout via runtime config flag.
description: Context: Certain open models (notably newer Qwen variants and some Llama forks) expose heterogeneous head layouts and intermittent head-wise padding which causes our existing prefetch+kernel selection logic to trigger suboptimal kernels, increased KV fragmentation, and occasional micro-stalls under continuous batching. Motivation: Reduce tail latency and token cost for mixed GQA/MQA traffic while preserving deterministic correctness. Summary: This change implements a hybrid prefetch holdback policy and a model-aware kernel-splitting pass that splits attention kernels into head-homogeneous subops at dispatch time when a heterogeneity signature is detected. The prefetch holdback introduces a small delay window to allow incoming batch items to better align head-dim distributions, avoiding premature KV prefetch that forces bloated KV slabs. Kernel-splitting ensures that when fragmentation is unavoidable we dispatch narrow, head-consistent kernels to preserve throughput without wasting compute on padded lanes. Design highlights: 1) New heterogeneity detector that samples the model metadata and early token traces (cheap checks only) to classify runs as homogeneous/heterogeneous. 2) Prefetch holdback: configurable window (default 2ms) that temporarily defers prefetch for head-misaligned batches; the window decays for low-latency SLO tenants. 3) Kernel-splitting pass: at plan generation we may emit 1..N sub-kernels, each tagged with head-mask metadata for the runtime scheduler to place on appropriate GPU lanes. 4) KV windowed-thresholds: tighten eviction and compaction thresholds for slabs affected by heterogeneous access patterns to reduce fragmentation over long-lived chat sessions. Backwards compatibility: All changes are guarded by runtime feature flags and default to conservative behavior for dedicated/private customers unless enabled. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for heterogeneity detector and splitting logic. - Integration tests with continuous batching harness covering MQA and GQA synthetic traces. - End-to-end perf runs against qwen-1.2 and llama-3-13b variants. Results are summarized below. Commits: initial prototype; detector refinements; kernel pass and scheduler hooks; perf tuning and config flags; tests and docs. Files touched include runtime scheduler, kernel planner, kv slab manager, baking harness and a short config schema addition. CI: full unit/integration/perf pipeline passed. Merge: squash and merge to main after two approvals. Motivation links: ENG-1938 notes on MQA tail-latency incidents; ENG-2045 prototype spike in bench lab.

discussion: Diego Martinez (review): This is a dense change — can you clarify the invariant guarantees of the split kernels vs original fused kernel?

Author (Priya Nair): The split kernels are semantically identical to the fused path; we only partition heads that are homogenous in dim and mask. I added comments and an assert in planner to ensure equivalence with a reference slow path in debug builds.
Sofia Chen (review): I saw a small perf regression on small-batch, low-latency tenants when the holdback was enabled. Can we gate by tenant SLO?
Author (Priya Nair): Yes, holdback is tenant-configurable and defaults to off for latency-sensitive tiers. Added a config override and unit test to validate gating.
